images.title: Walking around the Earth
images.purpose: Shows the estimate: 70 years of non-stop walking at 5 km an hour covers 3066000 km, about 76 times around the 40000 km Earth.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. One large plain circle for the Earth in the centre with a dashed path around it and four short labels around the circle.
images.exact_structure: One large circle filled light teal (#0072B2) with no map details. An amber (#E69F00) dashed ring just outside the circle with one arrowhead showing direction. Labels around it: '40000 km' beside the ring at the top, '5 km an hour' at the left, '70 years' at the right, '3066000 km' at the bottom. To the right of the circle, the label 'about 76 times' in a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly 1 circle, 1 ring, 1 box.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: State the assumptions, multiply them out, then divide by the distance around.
images.description: Shows the estimate: 70 years of non-stop walking at 5 km an hour covers 3066000 km, about 76 times around the 40000 km Earth.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which assumption, if changed, would change the answer most.

image_decisions.why: One clear picture of the assumptions and the result shows how an estimate is built.
